hero.title: Jain Councils: Canonical Codification
hero.description: An analytical study of the two major Jain Sanghas that preserved and codified the Jaina Agamas in ancient India.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: The evolution of the Jaina canon through two pivotal councils.

cards.details: First Jain Council held at Pataliputra under the patronage of Chandragupta Maurya to compile the 12 Angas.
Second Jain Council held at Valabhi, Gujarat, presided over by Devardhi Kshamashramana, finalizing the canon.

items.title: P-V (The Councils)

items.title: S-D (The Presidents)
items.decryption: S.D. for the Presidents. Sthulabhadra led the first, Devardhi the second.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing the Jain Councils with Buddhist Councils (Jain: Pataliputra/Valabhi; Buddhist: Rajagriha/Vaishali/Pataliputra/Kashmir).
Assuming the Jain canon was fully written down during the first council; it was largely oral until the second.
Incorrectly linking the first council with the rise of the Digambara sect exclusively; it was a collective effort before the final split.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Locations

  • Pataliputra (Magadha)
  • Valabhi (Gujarat)

Personalities

  • Sthulabhadra (First Council)
  • Devardhi Kshamashramana (Second)
  • First Council:
    • Patronage: Mauryan Empire.
    • Outcome: 12 Angas compiled.
    • Crisis: Bhadrabahu (leader of southern migration) rejected the results.
  • Second Council:
    • Context: Post-Gupta era.
    • Outcome: Final reduction of Jaina Agama to writing.
    • Significance: Shift from oral tradition (Shruti) to written scripture.
